items.headline: PPI excluding foods, energy and trade rose 0.5% in October; 12-month rate 4.9%
items.take: BLS reports final demand less foods, energy and trade rose 0.5% in October, the same as September, and 4.9% over the 12 months ended in October, versus 5.0% in September and 3.5% in October 2025 (Table A). AlphaGen read: the narrower gauge eased a tenth of a point on the year but remains well above its level a year ago.
items.source_name: BLS, Producer Price Index (October 2026)

items.headline: Compounded, PPI final demand rose about 5.7% from January through October
items.take: Compounding the seasonally adjusted monthly changes in BLS Table A for January through October 2026 (0.6, 0.5, 0.8, 1.1, 0.5, -0.1, 0.1, 0.4, 1.4 and 0.3 percent) gives a 5.7% rise in final demand prices. AlphaGen read: this is our calculation from rounded monthly figures and revised data, so treat it as approximate; BLS's own 12-month rate is 6.5%.
items.source_name: BLS, Producer Price Index (October 2026)

items.headline: PPI final demand energy edged down 0.1% in October after a 10.0% September jump
items.take: BLS says prices for final demand energy edged down 0.1% in October; its Table A shows the index rose 10.0% in September. Final demand goods less foods and energy rose 0.5% in October, against 0.3% in September. AlphaGen read: energy swung from the largest gain in Table A's final demand columns in September to a small decline, while headline final demand slowed from 1.4% to 0.3%.
items.source_name: BLS, Producer Price Index (October 2026)

items.headline: PPI headline now runs 1.6 points above the narrower measure, after trailing it a year ago
items.take: BLS Table A shows 12-month final demand inflation of 6.5% in October 2026 and 4.9% for final demand less foods, energy and trade, a gap of 1.6 percentage points by our calculation. In October 2025 the figures were 2.8% and 3.5%, a gap of -0.7 points. AlphaGen read: the headline index has moved from below to above the narrower measure, pointing to food, energy and trade components.
items.source_name: BLS, Producer Price Index (October 2026)

items.headline: NAR: pending home sales fell 4.7% in October and 16.7% from a year earlier
items.take: NAR's Nov. 18 release says pending home sales declined 4.7% month over month and 16.7% year over year in October, with declines in all four regions on both measures. AlphaGen read: contract signings, which lead closings, remain well below last year's pace.
items.source_name: National Association of Realtors, Pending Home Sales (October 2026)

items.headline: NAR pending sales: West -6.9% and South -6.3% in October, Northeast -0.8%
items.take: Month over month in October, NAR reports pending home sales fell 6.9% in the West, 6.3% in the South, 2.7% in the Midwest and 0.8% in the Northeast. Year over year, the West was down 20.3%, the South 18.7%, the Midwest 14.0% and the Northeast 11.1%. AlphaGen read: the South and West posted the largest drops on both measures.
items.source_name: National Association of Realtors, Pending Home Sales (October 2026)

items.headline: NAR's Yun says October could mark low point for contract signings as rates topped out
items.take: NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun said October could mark the low point in contract signings for this housing cycle, as mortgage rates appear to have topped out, and that the weak contract count points to sluggish fourth-quarter closings. FRED's Freddie Mac series shows the 30-year mortgage rate at 7.28% on Nov. 19, up from 7.11% on Nov. 12. AlphaGen read: the latest weekly rate rose, so the low-point case is NAR's view rather than something the rate data yet confirms.
items.source_name: National Association of Realtors and Freddie Mac, via FRED (MORTGAGE30US)

items.headline: NAR metros: Cincinnati pending sales -4.7% and Austin -9.7% from a year ago
items.take: In NAR's October release, which cites Realtor.com Economics data for the 50 largest metros, Cincinnati had the smallest year-over-year decline in pending sales at 4.7%, followed by Austin (9.7%), Hartford (10.0%), Indianapolis (11.3%) and Chicago (11.9%). AlphaGen read: even the best-performing large metros were down from a year earlier.
items.source_name: National Association of Realtors, Pending Home Sales (October 2026)

items.headline: ECB deposit facility rate moved to 2.25% on Jun. 17, then 2.50% on Sep. 16
items.take: FRED's ECB deposit facility rate series shows 2.00% from Jun. 11, 2025, then 2.25% on Jun. 17, 2026 and 2.50% on Sep. 16, 2026, still 2.50% on Nov. 23. AlphaGen read: the series records two increases this year after a year at 2.00%.
items.source_name: European Central Bank, via FRED (ECBDFR)

items.headline: EIA: U.S. energy 'stock change and other' was 0.4 quads in 2025, about 0.3% of supply
items.take: EIA's Nov. 17 note says its surveys put U.S. total primary energy supply and demand at about 128 quadrillion Btu each in 2025, with the stock change and other category at 0.4 quads, or about 0.3% of the total. EIA collects the data from over 60 surveys. AlphaGen read: the gap between reported supply and demand is small relative to the totals.
items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy

items.headline: EIA reconciles supply and demand with separate petroleum, natural gas and coal adjustment series
items.take: EIA says petroleum and biofuels use an adjustments series because survey responses may not precisely reflect actual activity, natural gas uses a balancing item series, and coal uses a losses and unaccounted for series. Biofuels also have a small balancing item for biodiesel supply and demand. AlphaGen read: each fuel is reconciled with its own series rather than one catch-all line.
items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy

items.headline: 10-year minus 2-year Treasury spread 0.29 points on Nov. 20, from 0.27 on Nov. 13
items.take: FRED's T10Y2Y series shows the 10-year minus 2-year Treasury constant-maturity spread at 0.29 percentage points on Nov. 20, versus 0.27 on Nov. 13. Daily readings that week ran from 0.27 (Nov. 18) to 0.30 (Nov. 17). AlphaGen read: the curve slope held within a three-hundredths-of-a-point band through the week.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (T10Y2Y)

items.headline: EIA lists causes of 'other' supply-demand differences, from timing to storage losses
items.take: EIA says the 'other' portion of stock change and other reflects differences in respondent reporting practices, timing between energy activity and reporting periods, measurement and estimation errors, limits in data collection systems and survey coverage, energy lost in transfers or storage, and unreported activities. EIA states these series are not a flaw in the underlying statistics and instead keep published data consistent and transparent. AlphaGen read: EIA also uses them to show the uncertainty around its survey data.
items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy

items.headline: Treasury lists 2-year Nov. 23, 5-year Nov. 24, 7-year Nov. 25 note auctions, all settling Nov. 30
items.take: Treasury's tentative auction schedule lists the 2-year note auction for Monday, Nov. 23, the 5-year for Tuesday, Nov. 24 and the 7-year for Wednesday, Nov. 25, all announced Nov. 19 and settling Monday, Nov. 30. The notes mature Nov. 30, 2028, Nov. 30, 2031 and Nov. 30, 2033. AlphaGen read: all three auctions fall within the Thanksgiving week and settle together on the first business day after it.
items.source_name: U.S. Treasury, Tentative Auction Schedule

items.headline: Treasury Nov. 24 auctions: 52-week and 6-week bills plus a 2-year FRN reopening
items.take: The tentative schedule lists three Treasury auctions for Tuesday, Nov. 24 alongside the 5-year note: a 52-week bill maturing Nov. 26, 2027, a 6-week bill maturing Jan. 7, 2027, and a reopening of the 2-year floating rate note maturing Oct. 31, 2028. All three were announced Nov. 19 and settle Friday, Nov. 27. AlphaGen read: the schedule has no offering-amount column, so sizes must come from each auction's announcement.
items.source_name: U.S. Treasury, Tentative Auction Schedule

items.headline: Treasury bill calendar: 4-, 8-, 17-week auctions Nov. 25; 13- and 26-week on Nov. 30
items.take: Treasury's tentative schedule lists 4-week, 8-week and 17-week bill auctions for Wednesday, Nov. 25, announced Nov. 24 and settling Tuesday, Dec. 1, with maturities of Dec. 29, 2026, Jan. 26, 2027 and Mar. 30, 2027. It lists 13-week and 26-week bill auctions for Monday, Nov. 30, announced Nov. 25 and settling Thursday, Dec. 3. AlphaGen read: the schedule is marked tentative, so the dates can change.
items.source_name: U.S. Treasury, Tentative Auction Schedule

items.headline: Fed calendar lists no Board speeches Nov. 23-30; Beige Book and data releases only
items.take: The Federal Reserve Board's November calendar shows speeches running through Nov. 20 and lists no speeches or testimony for Nov. 23 through Nov. 30. Entries in that span are statistical releases, such as H.6 Money Stock on Tuesday, Nov. 24 at 1:00 p.m., plus the Beige Book on Nov. 25 at 2:00 p.m. AlphaGen read: the calendar can be updated, so check it for added events.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board, Calendar: November 2026

items.headline: High-yield spread jumps 24 bp in a day to 3.76% on Nov. 20, highest since May 2025
items.take: The ICE BofA US High Yield Index option-adjusted spread was 3.76% on Nov. 20, up from 3.52% on Nov. 19 and 3.23% on Nov. 13, a 53 bp widening in five sessions (FRED). The last reading at or above 3.76% was 3.78% on May 1, 2025. The 24 bp one-day move was the largest in the Nov. 13-20 run, which had been widening 4 to 11 bp a day.
items.source_name: ICE BofA US High Yield Index OAS, FRED

items.headline: CCC spread reaches 14.02% on Nov. 20, highest in FRED's three-year window; BB at 2.29%
items.take: The ICE BofA CCC & Lower US High Yield spread rose to 14.02% on Nov. 20 from 13.61% on Nov. 19 and 13.16% on Nov. 13, the highest in the series' history on FRED, which starts Nov. 24, 2023. The BB spread went to 2.29% from 2.10% a day earlier and 1.86% on Nov. 13. The BB widening of 43 bp since Nov. 13 is about half the CCC's 86 bp, so stress is broadening but remains concentrated in the weakest credits.
items.source_name: ICE BofA CCC & Lower US High Yield Index OAS, FRED

items.headline: Investment-grade spread 0.98% on Nov. 20, up 9 bp in a week; BBB at 1.22%
items.take: The ICE BofA US Corporate Index option-adjusted spread was 0.98% on Nov. 20, up from 0.94% on Nov. 19 and 0.89% on Nov. 13 (FRED). The BBB spread was 1.22%, up from 1.17% and 1.11%. The last time the IG spread was at or above 0.98% was 1.02% on May 9, 2025, so the move is still modest next to the high-yield widening.
items.source_name: ICE BofA US Corporate Index OAS, FRED

items.headline: High-yield premium over investment grade widens to 2.78 points from 2.34
items.take: Subtracting the investment-grade spread (0.98%) from the high-yield spread (3.76%) on Nov. 20 gives a 2.78 percentage-point gap, against 2.34 points on Nov. 13 (3.23% less 0.89%), based on FRED's ICE BofA series. The gap, which shows how much extra compensation investors demand for lower-rated credit, grew by 44 bp in five sessions, with the high-yield leg accounting for 53 bp of widening and the IG leg 9 bp.
items.source_name: ICE BofA US High Yield and US Corporate Index OAS, FRED

items.headline: PRA insurer stress scenario: three weeks of catastrophes, cyber events and market stress
items.take: The PRA's 2026 DyGIST scenario was a sequence of severe yet plausible events over a three-week period in May 2026, including significant natural catastrophes and cyber events, coupled with a financial market stress. It was designed to push most of the 25 participating insurers beyond their internal risk appetite limits, and the responses included capital injections, credit facilities, dividend retention and significant reliance on reinsurance. AlphaGen read: the PRA stresses that the useful finding is whether those actions would be available and timely in a market-wide stress, not just the financial impact.
items.source_name: Bank of England (PRA)

items.headline: ECB DLT collateral: platforms must meet extra settlement-finality, outsourcing rules
items.take: The ECB said eligible DLT assets must meet all standard collateral criteria and be available through an eligible link to a central securities depository whose settlement system offers settlement in TARGET2-Securities. DLT platforms licensed under the EU DLT Pilot Regime also need to meet dedicated Eurosystem requirements, for example on settlement finality designation and outsourcing of critical functions, to be communicated in spring 2027. AlphaGen read: this builds on the Jan. 27, 2026 decision on assets issued in CSDs using DLT-based services, and keeps the existing collateral safeguards in place.
items.source_name: European Central Bank

items.headline: CrowdStrike-Zscaler: Qatalyst, BDT & MSD lead advisers; call moved up from Dec. 1
items.take: The release names Qatalyst Partners as sole lead financial advisor to CrowdStrike, with J.P. Morgan and BofA Securities also advising, and BDT & MSD Partners as sole lead financial advisor to Zscaler, with Citigroup and Goldman Sachs also named. The companies replaced a joint call previously scheduled for Dec. 1 with one held Nov. 23, and Zscaler separately reported fiscal first-quarter 2027 results the same day. AlphaGen read: the earlier call date lines the deal announcement up with both companies' results.
items.source_name: CrowdStrike Form 8-K Ex. 99.1 (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: Release: Zscaler protects 50% of the Fortune 500, handles 750B+ daily transactions
items.take: CrowdStrike's deal release says Zscaler protects 50 percent of the Fortune 500 and operates the world's largest distributed inline security cloud across more than 200 service locations. It adds that Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange processes more than 750 billion transactions per day, and that after closing device and network telemetry would converge into a single data set. AlphaGen read: these are CrowdStrike's characterizations of the target, and the data-combination plan is contingent on closing.
items.source_name: CrowdStrike Form 8-K Ex. 99.1 (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: CrowdStrike sees Zscaler adding over $185B to its addressable market by 2029
items.take: CrowdStrike estimates the Zscaler acquisition will expand its total addressable market by more than $185 billion in calendar year 2029, and says Zscaler would take it into network security, which it calls cybersecurity's largest single addressable market segment. Zscaler would be sold through CrowdStrike's system integrators, resellers, distributors and cloud marketplaces. AlphaGen read: the TAM figure is CrowdStrike's own estimate in the deal release, not an independent measure.
items.source_name: CrowdStrike Form 8-K Ex. 99.1 (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: CrowdStrike targets ~$1B revenue and $500M cost synergies from Zscaler deal
items.take: CrowdStrike said it expects revenue synergies to build over the first 30 months after close, reaching approximately $1 billion in annualized run-rate revenue, and $500 million in annualized run-rate cost synergies within 18 to 24 months of close. It expects the deal to be significantly and immediately accretive to free cash flow per share before synergies. AlphaGen read: these are company targets in the announcement, not results.
items.source_name: CrowdStrike and Zscaler joint press release (SEC 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

items.headline: Zscaler brings $3.9B ARR; combined ARR expected above $10B at close
items.take: The release cites Zscaler ARR of $3.9 billion as of its recently completed fiscal quarter and says the combined company is expected to begin with more than $10 billion in ARR. CrowdStrike said approximately 8,000 Zscaler customers are not yet CrowdStrike customers, and the two companies already share more than 2,000 customers. AlphaGen read: the cross-sell pool is the core of the strategic case.
items.source_name: CrowdStrike and Zscaler joint press release (SEC 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

items.headline: Zscaler founder, affiliates holding ~34% sign voting agreements for CrowdStrike deal
items.take: Jay Chaudhry and his affiliates, representing approximately 34% of Zscaler's outstanding shares, entered into voting agreements in support of the transaction. After closing, Chaudhry will continue to lead the Zscaler business and join the CrowdStrike Board of Directors; both companies operate independently until then. AlphaGen read: the transaction still needs Zscaler shareholder and regulatory approvals.
items.source_name: CrowdStrike and Zscaler joint press release (SEC 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

items.headline: CrowdStrike Q3 operating cash flow $665.2M vs $397.5M; cash $5.37B
items.take: CrowdStrike reported net cash generated from operations of $665.2 million in the quarter ended Oct. 31, 2026, compared with $397.5 million a year earlier, up 67.3% by AlphaGen's calculation. Cash and cash equivalents grew to $5.37 billion. AlphaGen read: the cash balance is a reference point for the company's stated all-stock structure in the Zscaler deal.
items.source_name: CrowdStrike Holdings Q3 FY2027 results (SEC 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

items.headline: CrowdStrike Q3 non-GAAP operating income $405.5M; subscription revenue $1.50B
items.take: CrowdStrike reported non-GAAP income from operations of $405.5 million versus $264.6 million a year earlier, up 53.3% by AlphaGen's calculation, while GAAP loss from operations narrowed to $0.8 million from $62.2 million. Subscription revenue was $1.50 billion, up 29%, and non-GAAP subscription gross margin was 82% versus 81%. AlphaGen read: the gap between GAAP and non-GAAP operating results remains wide.
items.source_name: CrowdStrike Holdings Q3 FY2027 results (SEC 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

items.headline: DoorDash Instacart term loan prices at SOFR + 1.00%; bridge cut to $11.208B
items.take: DoorDash's new $1.792 billion delayed draw term loan bears interest at Term SOFR plus an initial margin of 1.00%, with step-downs to 0.875% or 0.750% based on credit ratings, matures three years after funding, and carries a ticking fee of 0.08% to 0.10% a year from Feb. 25, 2027. The 364-day bridge commitment for the Instacart deal was cut from $13.0 billion to $11.208 billion. AlphaGen read: the bridge is a commitment, not drawn debt.
items.source_name: DoorDash, Inc. Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: BoE insurer stress test covered 25 firms, over 80% of UK general insurance market
items.take: The PRA's 2026 Dynamic General Insurance Stress Test used a scenario of severe insurance events over three weeks in May 2026, including natural catastrophes and cyber events, coupled with a financial market stress. The Bank of England says the exercise involved 25 major insurers representing more than 80% of the UK general insurance market, and that it was not a pass-or-fail exercise. AlphaGen read: the regulator frames the results as a test of crisis-response arrangements, not a verdict on capital adequacy.
items.source_name: Bank of England (PRA)

items.headline: Brent premium to WTI $3.41 on Nov. 17, from $3.12 on Nov. 12
items.take: FRED shows Brent at $92.94 and WTI at $89.53 on Nov. 17, a $3.41 gap by AlphaGen's calculation. On Nov. 12, Brent was $95.42 and WTI $92.30, a $3.12 gap. AlphaGen read: both benchmarks fell between the two dates and Brent fell by less than WTI, so the spread widened by $0.29.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (EIA data)

items.headline: ECB plans June 2027 start for DLT-asset collateral; platform rules due spring 2027
items.take: The ECB says the Eurosystem expects to communicate dedicated requirements for DLT platforms in spring 2027, with implementation planned to take effect in June 2027. Eligible assets must be made available through a link to a central securities depository operating an eligible securities settlement system that offers settlement in TARGET2-Securities. The decision follows the Jan. 27, 2026 announcement on accepting assets issued in CSDs using DLT-based services. AlphaGen read: the timeline puts any collateral use of these assets well after today's approval.
items.source_name: European Central Bank

items.headline: Sept. trade: goods deficit $135.9B offset by $30.9B services surplus for $105.0B gap
items.take: BEA and Census reported a September goods and services deficit of $105.0 billion, down $0.7 billion from a revised $105.7 billion in August. The goods deficit decreased $0.7 billion to $135.9 billion and the services surplus decreased by less than $0.1 billion to $30.9 billion; exports were $321.5 billion and imports $426.6 billion. AlphaGen read: $135.9 billion less $30.9 billion reconciles to the $105.0 billion headline, so services offset about 23% of the goods gap. The next release is Dec. 8.
items.source_name: U.S. Census Bureau and BEA

items.headline: BEA Nov. 25, 8:30 a.m. ET: Q3 GDP second estimate and October PCE on the same morning
items.take: BEA's schedule lists the Q3 GDP second estimate with corporate profits and the October personal income and outlays report, including PCE, for Wednesday, Nov. 25 at 8:30 a.m. ET. The advance estimate showed real GDP up 3.4% at an annualized rate. AlphaGen read: growth and inflation data from the same agency land together on the day before Thanksgiving.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis

items.headline: CrowdStrike agrees to acquire Zscaler in all-stock deal valued at about $43.9B
items.take: CrowdStrike and Zscaler announced a definitive agreement on Nov. 23 under which Zscaler holders receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per share, valuing Zscaler at approximately $43.9 billion. The release puts the implied value at about $260.41 per Zscaler share, a premium of approximately 34%, with CrowdStrike holders expected to own about 84.1% of the combined company and closing expected in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028, subject to Zscaler shareholder and regulatory approvals. AlphaGen read: the exchange ratio is fixed, so the headline value moves with CrowdStrike's share price until closing.
items.source_name: CrowdStrike and Zscaler joint press release (SEC 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

items.headline: CrowdStrike Q3 revenue $1.58B, up 28%; ending ARR $6.26B, up 27%
items.take: CrowdStrike reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 total revenue of $1.58 billion, up 28% from $1.23 billion a year earlier, with ending ARR of $6.26 billion as of Oct. 31 and net new ARR of $419.2 million. Free cash flow was $474.4 million versus $295.9 million a year earlier, up 60.3% by AlphaGen's calculation. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.02 against a loss of $0.03; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.34 versus $0.24.
items.source_name: CrowdStrike Q3 FY2027 results (SEC 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

items.headline: CrowdStrike lifts FY27 outlook: revenue $6,078.1M-$6,084.1M, EPS $1.28
items.take: CrowdStrike's guidance for the year ending Jan. 31, 2027 calls for total revenue of $6,078.1 million to $6,084.1 million and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.28, with fourth-quarter revenue of $1,638.1 million to $1,644.1 million and EPS of $0.36. The company said it increased fiscal 2027 net new ARR growth guidance by 1,060 basis points to 45% at the midpoint. AlphaGen read: the pending Zscaler acquisition is not expected to close until the second half of fiscal 2028.
items.source_name: CrowdStrike Q3 FY2027 results (SEC 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

items.headline: DoorDash upsizes revolver to $3.5B and adds $1.792B loan for Instacart deal
items.take: In an 8-K filed Nov. 23, DoorDash said a commitment increase raised its revolving credit commitments by $1.5 billion, from $2.0 billion to $3.5 billion, maturing Aug. 5, 2031. It also entered a $1.792 billion senior unsecured delayed draw term loan tied to its pending acquisition of Maplebear Inc. (Instacart), which can be increased to as much as $2.0 billion. AlphaGen read: the term loan is committed financing for the Instacart merger signed Oct. 28, not new debt already drawn.
items.source_name: DoorDash, Inc. Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: ECB to accept DLT-issued assets as eligible Eurosystem collateral
items.take: The ECB Governing Council approved accepting marketable assets issued on DLT platforms licensed under the EU DLT Pilot Regime Regulation, and available on TARGET2-Securities, as eligible collateral for Eurosystem credit operations. The assets must meet all standard eligibility criteria, and the Eurosystem expects to communicate dedicated platform requirements in spring 2027. AlphaGen read: this is a collateral-framework change, not a monetary policy decision.
items.source_name: European Central Bank press release

items.headline: BoE stress test: reinsurance cut insurers' gross scenario losses by about 72%
items.take: The Prudential Regulation Authority published results of its 2026 Dynamic General Insurance Stress Test (DyGIST) on Nov. 23, involving 25 major insurers representing more than 80% of the UK general insurance market. Reinsurance reduced gross losses from the insurance events by around 72% in the scenario of catastrophes, cyber events and financial market stress. AlphaGen read: the PRA's emphasis was on testing crisis and recovery plans, including concentrations in reinsurance and group-support arrangements.
items.source_name: Bank of England / PRA news release

items.headline: GBP/USD at 1.3212 on Nov. 13 is 2.71 cents below its Nov. 5 reading of 1.3483
items.take: FRED's daily Federal Reserve H.10 series shows the dollar buying 1.3212 per pound (USD per GBP) on Nov. 13, versus 1.3483 on Nov. 5 and 1.3459 on Nov. 4. That is the lowest reading in the Nov. 2 to Nov. 13 window of observations. AlphaGen read: the pound's slide over the second week of November ran alongside a 2-year Treasury yield that rose to 4.88% on Nov. 13 from 4.51% on Nov. 6.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board H.10 via FRED (DEXUSUK)

items.headline: Yuan steady: 6.6710 per dollar on Nov. 13 within a 6.6680 to 6.6760 band since Nov. 3
items.take: FRED's H.10 series shows 6.6710 Chinese yuan per U.S. dollar on Nov. 13, after 6.6704 on Nov. 12 and 6.6760 on Nov. 6. Every observation from Nov. 3 to Nov. 13 sits between 6.6680 and 6.6760, a spread of 0.0080. AlphaGen read: the 0.0080 spread over eight observations is narrow, with no breakout in the series.

items.headline: 2-year Treasury at 4.76% on Nov. 19 is 76 bp above the top of the 3.75%-4.00% fed funds range
items.take: FRED shows the 2-year constant-maturity yield at 4.76% on Nov. 19, versus the 4.00% upper bound of the fed funds target range and a 3.88% effective rate. The 2-year was 4.51% on Nov. 6 and peaked at 4.88% on Nov. 13 in that window.
