items.headline: Lagarde: digital euro aimed at 2029 issuance if law passes by end-2026
items.take: In a Nov. 20 speech in Frankfurt, ECB President Christine Lagarde said international card schemes handle more than 60% of euro area card payments and 14 of the 21 euro area countries have no domestic scheme. She said that if legislation is adopted by the end of this year, the ECB aims to be ready for a first digital euro issuance in 2029. For Europe, the payments push is a sovereignty argument as much as a technology one.
items.source_name: European Central Bank

items.headline: Lagarde: tokenised assets ~€23B in March; ESM settled €1B bond on Pontes
items.take: Lagarde said the market for tokenised assets was worth around €23 billion worldwide in March, five times its size a year earlier. The ECB launched Pontes in September to settle tokenised transactions in central bank money, and the European Stability Mechanism settled a €1 billion digitally native bond on it earlier this month. The ECB is positioning settlement infrastructure as the common standard before platforms diverge.
items.source_name: European Central Bank

items.headline: Lagarde: EUREP repo facility made permanent in February; 30+ central banks interested
items.take: Lagarde said the ECB made EUREP, its repo facility for central banks, permanent in February and open to central banks worldwide, and that more than 30 central banks have already expressed interest. She also cited the linking of TIPS with fast payment systems in other regions and work to keep swap lines fit for purpose. The measures are aimed at making the euro easier to use abroad.
items.source_name: European Central Bank

items.headline: Merck: Glocer to retire from board in May 2027; Baker named lead director
items.take: Merck said Thomas H. Glocer intends to retire from its Board at the May 2027 Annual Meeting of Shareholders. The independent directors appointed Douglas M. Baker, Jr., a director since 2022, as independent lead director effective Jan. 1, 2027. The announcement was a governance change and did not include financial guidance.
items.source_name: Merck & Co. (SEC Form 8-K, Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: Air Products to nominate Carol Williams; two directors won't stand in 2027
items.take: Air Products said it will nominate Carol Williams, who spent 34 years at Dow, as an independent director candidate at its 2027 Annual Meeting. It also said Jessica Trocchi Graziano and Bhavesh (Bob) Patel will not stand for re-election and will retire when their terms conclude. The board refresh is the substance of the release; no financial figures were given.
items.source_name: Air Products and Chemicals (SEC Form 8-K, Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: FRED: 10-year yield 0.73 point above 3-month bill on Nov. 18, from 0.78 on Nov. 16
items.take: FRED shows the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.07% and the 3-month yield at 4.34% on Nov. 18, a gap of 0.73 percentage point. On Nov. 16 the 10-year was 5.12% and the 3-month 4.34%, a 0.78-point gap; on Nov. 13 it was 5.15% against 4.32%, or 0.83. The gap narrowed because the 10-year fell while the bill yield held, a bond-market move that left short-term rates anchored.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: FRED: 2-year yield 0.46 point above 3-month bill on Nov. 18; 2-year 4.80%
items.take: FRED reports the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.80% and the 3-month at 4.34% on Nov. 18, so the 2-year sits 0.46 percentage point higher (AlphaGen calculation). The 2-year was 4.88% on Nov. 13 against a 4.32% bill, a 0.56-point gap. A narrower gap means the market is pricing a less steep path for short-term rates than it was a few days ago.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: Core CPI index 339.900 in October, up 0.30%; 3-month pace 3.7% annualized
items.take: FRED's seasonally adjusted CPI excluding food and energy (1982-84=100) was 339.900 in October, up 0.30% from 338.896 in September; September's gain was 0.33%. Since July's 336.789 the index has risen 0.92%, or 3.7% at an annual rate (AlphaGen calculation). Core prices are still rising at a pace above the Fed's 2% goal.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: Industrial production index 103.395 in October, down 0.43% on the month, up 2.1% on the year
items.take: FRED's total industrial production index (2017=100) was 103.3954 in October, down 0.43% from 103.8458 in September, after a 0.73% rise in September. Against October 2025's 101.2195 it is up 2.1% (AlphaGen calculations). Factory, mining and utility output slipped in October but remains above its year-earlier level.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: Germany's 10-year yield 3.42% in October, down from 3.47%; UK 1.92 points higher
items.take: FRED's OECD-sourced long-term government bond series shows Germany at 3.42% in October, down from 3.47% in September and up from 2.62% a year earlier. The UK reading was 5.34%, which puts it 1.92 percentage points above Germany, versus 1.77 in September (AlphaGen calculations). British borrowing costs have risen faster than German ones over the past month.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: Bath & Body Works Q3 net sales $1,577M, down 1.0%; diluted EPS $0.19 vs $0.37
items.take: Bath & Body Works reported third-quarter net sales of $1,577 million versus $1,594 million, a decrease of 1.0%, with operating income of $108 million versus $161 million. Diluted EPS was $0.19 versus $0.37; adjusted diluted EPS was $0.26 versus $0.35. Lower operating income on slightly lower sales shows costs outpacing revenue in the quarter.
items.source_name: Bath & Body Works (GlobeNewswire release)

items.headline: Bath & Body Works: stores down 4.3%, direct up 2.6%, international up 39.3% in Q3
items.take: Q3 sales in U.S. and Canada stores were $1,169 million versus $1,222 million (-4.3%), direct U.S. and Canada sales were $307 million versus $299 million (+2.6%), and International and Other was $101 million versus $73 million (+39.3%). Stores still made up about 74% of Q3 net sales ($1,169M of $1,577M), so store traffic remains the main swing factor.
items.source_name: Bath & Body Works (GlobeNewswire release)

items.headline: Bath & Body Works raises FY26 sales outlook; sees net sales down 3.4% to 2.1%
items.take: The company now expects fiscal 2026 net sales to decline between 3.4% and 2.1% versus $7,291 million in fiscal 2025, and Q4 net sales to decline between 5.5% and 2.0% versus $2,724 million, with Q4 diluted EPS of $1.41 to $1.61. It also announced a new $500 million share repurchase program that may begin after the existing January 2025 program is completed. Even the raised full-year range still implies lower sales than last year.
items.source_name: Bath & Body Works (GlobeNewswire release)

items.headline: Fed publishes revised 2027 FOMC schedule: eight meetings, Oct. 26-27 set for strategy
items.take: The Federal Reserve's revised tentative 2027 schedule, released Nov. 12, lists meetings on Jan. 26-27, Mar. 16-17, Apr. 27-28, Jun. 8-9, Jul. 27-28, Sep. 14-15, Oct. 26-27 and Nov. 16-17, with the first 2028 meeting on Jan. 25-26. The Committee will announce its decision on the second day of each meeting except Oct. 26-27, which is dedicated to broad monetary policy strategy issues. The calendar fixes the dates markets will watch for 2027 rate decisions.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board

items.headline: CPI all-items index up 1.4% in three months to October, a 5.7% annual pace
items.take: FRED's seasonally adjusted CPI index was 337.476 in October, up 0.35% from 336.298 in September and 1.40% from 332.813 in July. Compounded over four quarters, the July–October gain equals a 5.7% annual rate. AlphaGen read: the headline index has run well ahead of the core index, which rose 0.92% over the same three months, a 3.7% annual pace.
items.source_name: BLS Consumer Price Index via FRED (CPIAUCSL, CPILFESL)

items.headline: Core PCE index 130.902 in September, up 0.32% on the month
items.take: FRED's core PCE price index (excluding food and energy) was 130.902 in September, up from 130.489 in August and 129.969 in June. That is a 0.32% monthly gain and a 2.9% annualized pace over June–September. AlphaGen read: core PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, has been running below the 3.7% annualized pace of core CPI over July–October, though the two cover different months and baskets.
items.source_name: BEA Personal Consumption Expenditures via FRED (PCEPILFE)

items.headline: Unemployment rate 4.1% in October, 7.1M unemployed; range 4.1%–4.3% since March
items.take: BLS said the unemployment rate changed little at 4.1% in October and the number of unemployed people, at 7.1 million, was little changed. The rate has stayed in a narrow range of 4.1% to 4.3% since March, and FRED shows 4.2% in September and 4.1% in July and August. AlphaGen read: a labor market that is not loosening keeps the Fed's focus on inflation.
items.source_name: BLS Employment Situation, October 2026

items.headline: BBB corporate spread 1.16 points on Nov. 18, up from 1.11 on Nov. 13
items.take: FRED's ICE BofA BBB option-adjusted spread was 1.16 percentage points on Nov. 18, up from 1.12 on Nov. 16, 1.15 on Nov. 17 and 1.11 on Nov. 13. The broad investment-grade index spread was 0.93 on Nov. 18, so BBB paper carried 0.23 point more than the index. AlphaGen read: the BBB gap widened 5 basis points in three sessions.
items.source_name: ICE Data Indices via FRED (BAMLC0A4CBBB, BAMLC0A0CM)

items.take: Census says that effective with the November 2026 advance release for the third quarter of 2026, not seasonally adjusted Quarterly Services estimates were revised for historical corrections and the 2023 and 2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey results. The seasonally adjusted Selected Services Total was also revised, with new seasonal factors. AlphaGen read: BEA uses the survey in its GDP estimates, so the revisions bear on the Nov. 25 GDP second estimate.
items.source_name: U.S. Census Bureau, Quarterly Services Survey

The Treasury General Account was $916,613M, up $2,243M on the week but $83,114M below its Oct. 28 level. AlphaGen read: the model-based Q4 reading sits close to Q3's, though it is an estimate that changes with each data release, not an official statistic.

items.take: The IMF global aluminum price on FRED was $3,283.05 a tonne in September, up $32.93 from August's $3,250.12 and 23.7% above September 2025's $2,654.48. AlphaGen read: the price peaked at $3,658.22 in May and is $375.17 below that level.

items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, Release Schedule

Cook's speech "The U.S. Economy in Global Context" at the Annual Conference of the Central Bank of Chile in Santiago at 12:15 p.m. the same day. items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board, Calendar: November 2026

items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, Release Schedule

items.take: FRED shows the 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield at 5.07% on Nov. 18, down from 5.10% on Nov. 17 and 5.15% on Nov. 13. items.take: FRED's 10-year minus 2-year Treasury constant-maturity spread was 0.28 percentage point on Nov. 19, up from 0.27 on Nov. 18 and below 0.30 on Nov. 17. The spread has stayed between 0.24 and 0.30 point in the dated observations from Nov. 12 to Nov. 19. AlphaGen read: the curve has been steady in a narrow range over the past week.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED), T10Y2Y

items.headline: FRED: Fed reverse repo usage $0.405B on Nov. 19, up from $0.331B a day earlier
items.take: FRED shows overnight reverse repurchase agreement usage at the Federal Reserve at $0.405 billion on Nov. 19, up from $0.331 billion on Nov. 18 and $0.351 billion on Nov. 17. Usage was $0.250 billion on Nov. 12. AlphaGen read: usage stayed below $0.5 billion on every dated observation shown from Nov. 12 to Nov. 19.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED), RRPONTSYD

items.take: FRED shows SOFR at 3.90% on Nov. 18, down from 3.92% on Nov. 17, while the 2-year Treasury yield was 4.80%, a gap of 0.90 percentage point versus 0.88 a day earlier. AlphaGen read: a 2-year yield above the overnight rate points to markets pricing short-term rates higher than today's.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED), SOFR and DGS2

items.headline: FRED: 30-year yield 0.34 pt above 10-year on Nov. 18, versus 0.36 a day earlier
items.take: FRED shows the 30-year Treasury yield at 5.41% and the 10-year at 5.07% on Nov. 18, a gap of 0.34 percentage point, down from 0.36 on Nov. 17 (5.46% and 5.10%). The 30-year fell 5 basis points on the day, against 3 for the 10-year. AlphaGen read: the long end fell a bit more than the 10-year.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED), DGS30

items.headline: Intuit agrees to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68B in cash
items.take: In an 8-K, Intuit said it entered an Equity and Asset Purchase Agreement on Nov. 19 to sell its Mailchimp business to Bending Spoons US Inc. for an all-cash base purchase price of $3.68 billion, subject to customary adjustments. Intuit also agreed to invest about $368 million of the purchase price in Bending Spoons S.p.A. for 8,818,595 newly issued ordinary shares, and closing is expected in early calendar 2027. AlphaGen read: the reinvestment equals 10% of the base price, so Intuit's net cash from the sale would be lower than the headline figure.
items.source_name: Intuit Inc., Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: 30-year mortgage rate 7.28% on Nov. 19, up from 7.11% a week earlier
items.take: FRED's series for Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey shows the 30-year fixed rate at 7.28% on Nov. 19, up 0.17 percentage point from 7.11% on Nov. 12. It had been 7.18% on Nov. 5 and 7.24% on Oct. 29. AlphaGen read: the weekly reading reverses the declines of the prior three weeks and returns to roughly the late-October level.
items.source_name: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey, via FRED (MORTGAGE30US)

items.headline: Fed total assets $6.741T on Nov. 18, down $17.4B from a week earlier
items.take: FRED's weekly series for Federal Reserve total assets (WALCL) shows $6,741,452 million on Nov. 18, versus $6,758,867 million on Nov. 11, a decline of $17.4 billion. The Nov. 4 level was $6,748,145 million. AlphaGen read: the balance sheet is little changed over the four weeks shown, moving within a range of about $17 billion.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board H.4.1, via FRED (WALCL)

items.headline: Duke Energy sells $875M of 6.05% senior notes due 2036
items.take: Duke Energy filed an underwriting agreement dated Nov. 17, 2026 for $875,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 6.05% Senior Notes due 2036, with MUFG, PNC, Santander, SMBC Nikko, U.S. Bancorp and Wells Fargo as representatives of the underwriters. The agreement was filed as Exhibit 99.1 to an 8-K. AlphaGen read: a 6.05% coupon on a 10-year utility note is a reference point for borrowing costs in a sector with heavy capital spending.
items.source_name: Duke Energy Corporation, Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: Edwards Lifesciences signs new $750M five-year revolving credit facility
items.take: Edwards Lifesciences said on Nov. 19 it entered an Amended and Restated Five Year Credit Agreement providing a $750 million multi-currency unsecured revolving facility maturing Nov. 19, 2031, with an option to add up to $375 million more. Borrowings bear interest at SOFR or a base rate plus a margin based on leverage ratio or debt ratings. AlphaGen read: the company describes the move as a planned refreshment of its bank facility, replacing the July 2022 agreement.
items.source_name: Edwards Lifesciences Corp., Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: 10-year breakeven inflation rate 2.16% on Nov. 19, down from 2.24% on Nov. 13
items.take: FRED's 10-year breakeven inflation rate was 2.16% on Nov. 19, from 2.19% on Nov. 18 and 2.24% on Nov. 13, a drop of 0.08 percentage point over the six observations shown. The 10-year TIPS real yield was 2.88% on Nov. 18 versus 2.91% on Nov. 13. AlphaGen read: this market-based inflation measure has eased through the week while real yields stayed near 2.9%.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED (T10YIE, DFII10)

items.headline: Nike director Mónica Gil resigns; board shrinks to eleven
items.take: Nike said in an 8-K that director Mónica Gil notified the company on Nov. 13 of her decision to resign from the Board and its Compensation Committee, effective Nov. 19, reducing the Board to eleven directors. The filing says her decision is not because of a disagreement with the company or the Board on any matter relating to operations, policies or practices. AlphaGen read: the filing describes no replacement director.
items.source_name: NIKE, Inc., Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: Banks' net tightening of C&I loan standards 1.7% in Oct survey, from 0.0% in July
items.take: FRED's series for the Fed's Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey shows a net 1.7% of domestic banks tightening standards on commercial and industrial loans to large and middle-market firms in the October 2026 reading, up from 0.0% in July and 8.1% in April. A year earlier, in October 2025, the figure was 6.5%. AlphaGen read: the net share is small and positive, so on this measure credit standards for large firms are close to unchanged rather than tightening broadly.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey, via FRED (DRTSCILM)

items.headline: ECB deposit rate 2.50% on Nov. 19 vs. U.S. effective fed funds 3.88% on Nov. 18
items.take: The European Central Bank's deposit facility rate stood at 2.50% on Nov. 19, according to FRED, while the U.S. effective federal funds rate was 3.88% on Nov. 18, the latest reading in the FRED series. That is a gap of 1.38 percentage points. AlphaGen read: the two central banks' policy rates remain well apart, and the dates differ by a day because the series update on different schedules.
items.source_name: European Central Bank, via FRED (ECBDFR); Federal Reserve Board, via FRED (DFF)

items.headline: Global copper price $14,473 a tonne in September, up 44.8% from a year earlier
items.take: FRED's monthly global copper price series, sourced from the IMF, was $14,473.06 per metric ton in September 2026, up 1.0% from $14,331.26 in August and 44.8% above $9,994.79 in September 2025. Aluminum in the same data set was $3,283.05 per metric ton, up 1.0% on the month and 23.7% on the year. AlphaGen read: industrial metals prices have risen sharply over the past year, which is a cost input for manufacturers and construction.
items.source_name: International Monetary Fund global commodity prices, via FRED (PCOPPUSDM, PALUMUSDM)

items.headline: Global wheat price $246.85 a tonne in September, up 59.1% on the year; maize $236.92
items.take: FRED's monthly IMF-sourced series show the global wheat price at $246.85 per metric ton in September 2026, up 3.8% from August and 59.1% above $155.12 in September 2025. The global maize price was $236.92 per metric ton, up 7.1% on the month and 20.8% on the year. AlphaGen read: both grain prices were higher in September than in July and August in these series, which can feed into food costs with a lag.
items.source_name: International Monetary Fund global commodity prices, via FRED (PWHEAMTUSDM, PMAIZMTUSDM)

items.headline: New-home supply 8.4 months at the Sept. sales pace, from 8.5 in August
items.take: FRED's Census series for monthly supply of new houses was 8.4 months in September 2026, down from 8.5 in August and 8.9 in July, and above 8.2 months in September 2025. AlphaGen read: supply stays above eight months at the current sales pace, and the slight decline in August and September is a small move.
items.source_name: U.S. Census Bureau and HUD, via FRED (MSACSR)

items.headline: Jefferson: if price pressures are contained, prioritizing employment risks may be prudent
items.take: Vice Chair Jefferson said on Nov. 19 that "if price pressures are contained, it may be prudent to prioritize downside risks to employment," after saying a stronger reaction to inflation is warranted if expectations risk becoming unanchored. He called the energy price shock tied to the conflict in the Middle East a case where the inflation and output-gap objectives pull in opposite directions. AlphaGen read: the speech sets out a two-sided condition, with inflation expectations as the dividing line, rather than a stated policy direction.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board (Vice Chair Jefferson speech, Nov. 19, 2026)

items.headline: Jefferson: energy, trade and AI shocks are all unfolding at once
items.take: Vice Chair Jefferson said in his Nov. 19 speech that "energy, trade, and AI shocks are all unfolding at once" and that Fed colleagues and peers abroad must weigh them simultaneously. He said that in the future, advancements in productivity "could exert downward pressure on inflation while continuing to support growth," while the AI buildout currently exerts upward pressure on demand and inflation. AlphaGen read: the speech separates what AI is doing to prices now from what it might do later.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board (Vice Chair Jefferson speech, Nov. 19, 2026)

items.headline: 5-year breakeven inflation rate 2.23% on Nov. 18, down from 2.30% on Nov. 13
items.take: FRED shows the 5-year breakeven inflation rate at 2.23% on Nov. 18, versus 2.26% on Nov. 17, 2.25% on Nov. 16 and 2.30% on Nov. 13; its recent high in this window was 2.31% on Nov. 12. items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (T5YIE)

items.take: FRED shows reserve balances with Federal Reserve Banks at $2,960,603 million on Nov. 11, up $30.5 billion from $2,930,088 million on Nov. 4 and below $3,029,659 million on Oct. 7. items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (WRESBAL; WTREGEN)

items.take: FRED shows the Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index at -0.478 for the week ended Nov. 13, versus -0.473 on Nov. 6, -0.470 on Oct. 30 and -0.507 on Sept. 25. items.take: FRED shows the U.S. dollar-to-pound exchange rate at $1.3212 per pound on Nov. 13, compared with $1.3240 on Nov. 12, $1.3322 on Nov. 10 and $1.3483 on Nov. 5. items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (DEXUSUK, Board of Governors H.10)

items.headline: Philly Fed factory index falls to 6.3 in November from 20.9 in October
items.take: The Philadelphia Fed's November Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey, released Nov. 19, put the current general activity index at 6.3, down from 20.9 in October; the Fed's summary says it fell to a six-month low but remained positive. Survey responses were collected Nov. 9 to 16. AlphaGen read: a positive index still points to expansion in the region's factories, but the drop is large for one month.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey

items.headline: Philly Fed: prices paid index 58.2, prices received 47.0 in November
items.take: In the Philadelphia Fed's November survey, the prices paid index rose to 58.2 from 43.2 in October and the prices received index rose to 47.0 from 40.1. The survey text says both price indexes increased from already elevated readings. AlphaGen read: it adds regional input-cost evidence alongside the October CPI and PPI data already out.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey

items.headline: Philly Fed: employment index 11.6; future activity index 33.6 in November
items.take: The Philadelphia Fed's November survey showed the employment index at 11.6, up from 9.1 in October, and the future general activity index at 33.6 versus 33.0 in October. The Fed notes most future indicators declined but still suggest expectations for overall growth over the next six months. AlphaGen read: firms still expect growth even as the current activity index cooled.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey

items.headline: Philly Fed: 56.0% of firms expect cost changes; 78.6% see rivals raising prices
items.take: In the Philadelphia Fed's November special questions, 56.0% of manufacturers anticipate near-term changes in industry costs, up from 44% last quarter, and 42.3% say core customers became more price sensitive since last quarter. Among firms expecting cost changes, 78.6% expect competitors to raise prices, with a median expected timing of 3.0 months. AlphaGen read: firms see cost pressure spreading to selling prices, though customers are pushing back.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey

items.headline: Rivian's Class B stock converted to Class A; ten-vote shares end
items.take: Rivian said in an 8-K that on Nov. 15 the 3,912,500 outstanding Class B shares automatically converted one-for-one into Class A stock on the five-year anniversary of its IPO, and about 1,459,886,616 Class A shares were outstanding afterward. Class B carried ten votes per share; Class A carries one. AlphaGen read: the filing says the conversion had no impact on economic interests or total shares outstanding, but it ends the high-vote class.
items.source_name: SEC EDGAR, Rivian Automotive Form 8-K

items.headline: ADP says it has acquired ZenBusiness, adding business formation and compliance
items.take: ADP said Nov. 19 that it has acquired ZenBusiness, a formation and compliance services business founded in 2015 and based in Austin, Texas, which the release says has helped over one million entrepreneurs. The release does not state a price, financing or closing timeline, and describes the deal as completed. AlphaGen read: it adds formation and compliance to a small-business base that ADP puts at more than 980,000 clients.
items.source_name: ADP, Inc. (PR Newswire release)

items.headline: Freddie Mac: 15-year mortgage rate 6.45%; 30-year 7.11% vs 6.24% a year ago
items.take: Freddie Mac's survey for the week ended Nov. 12 put the 15-year fixed rate at 6.45%, down from 6.57% the prior week and up from 5.49% a year ago. The 30-year rate was 7.11%, from 7.18% last week and 6.24% a year ago, a fourth consecutive weekly decline that Freddie Mac called the lowest in seven weeks. AlphaGen calculation: the 30-year rate is 0.87 percentage point above a year ago and the 15-year rate 0.96 point above. The Nov. 19 release was not yet posted on the page when read.
items.source_name: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey

items.headline: BLS: October payrolls showed little change in retail, construction, government and more
items.take: BLS said October employment showed little change in mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction; construction; wholesale trade; retail trade; information; financial activities; social assistance; leisure and hospitality; other services; and government. The 165,000 total gain came from professional and business services, health care, and transportation and warehousing, with manufacturing up 19,000. AlphaGen read: the report's strength was concentrated in a few industries rather than spread across the economy.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics

items.headline: BLS: professional and business services has added 269,000 jobs since October 2025 low
items.take: BLS's October jobs report says professional and business services has added 269,000 jobs since a recent low in October 2025, after a 70,000 gain in October against a 12-month average of 15,000. Within the sector, professional, scientific, and technical services rose 33,000 and management of companies and enterprises rose 9,000. AlphaGen read: the sector went from a low last October to the largest single-month contributor to October's 165,000 payroll gain.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics

items.headline: Walmart Q3 revenue $188.8B, up 5.2%; company raises FY27 outlook
items.take: Walmart reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $188.8 billion, up 5.2%, or 4.5% in constant currency, and said it is raising its outlook for fiscal 2027. Operating income rose $1.1 billion, or 16.0%, and was up 5.5% on an adjusted constant-currency basis. The release page does not show the new guidance ranges, so the size of the raise is not confirmed here.
items.source_name: Walmart Inc. (Business Wire release)

items.headline: Walmart Q3: global eCommerce up 17%, advertising up 25%, membership fees up 17%
items.take: Walmart said global eCommerce sales grew 17%, led by store-fulfilled pickup and delivery, with Walmart U.S. eCommerce up 23%. Global advertising rose 25% (Walmart U.S. 37%) and membership fee revenue grew 17% globally. The company also launched a U.S. membership bundle combining Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus for $120 annually.
items.source_name: Walmart Inc. (Business Wire release)

items.headline: Walmart Q3 GAAP EPS $0.62, adjusted EPS $0.65; gross profit rate up 28 bps
items.take: Walmart reported GAAP EPS of $0.62 and adjusted EPS of $0.65 for the third quarter; the adjusted figure excludes a net loss of $0.03, net of tax, on equity and other investments. The gross profit rate rose 28 basis points, led by Walmart U.S. The release page gives no prior-year EPS, so the year-over-year change is not computed here.
items.source_name: Walmart Inc. (Business Wire release)

items.headline: Walmart: inventory up 8.1%, $6.5B long-term debt issued, ROI 15.4%
items.take: Walmart said global inventory was up 8.1%, which it attributed to strategic initiatives, timing of seasonal events and cost inflation. It issued $6.5 billion of long-term debt for general corporate purposes, and reported return on assets of 7.2% and return on investment of 15.4%. Inventory growing faster than the 5.2% revenue gain is something to watch in the 10-Q.
items.source_name: Walmart Inc. (Business Wire release)

items.headline: Fed issues consent cease-and-desist order against former First Security Bancorp employee
items.take: The Federal Reserve Board announced a consent cease-and-desist order against a former employee of First Security Bancorp, citing breach of fiduciary duty and violation of Regulation W. The release, issued Nov. 19 at 11:00 a.m. EST, was revised the same day to correct the action type to a consent cease-and-desist order from a consent prohibition.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board

items.headline: BoE market group: UK resilience strengthened case for higher rates
items.take: Minutes of the Bank of England Market Participants Group meeting of Nov. 18, published Nov. 19, say participants saw UK growth resilience this year despite the energy shock as having broadly strengthened the case for higher rates, with the November increase widely expected. They also discussed AI-related capex, rising debt financing, hedge-fund leverage and sovereign debt pressures. The group is a listening forum rather than a policy decision, so the minutes show what market participants told the MPC, not what the MPC plans.
items.source_name: Bank of England

items.headline: 30-year mortgage rate 7.11% on Nov. 12, from 7.40% in early October
items.take: FRED data show the 30-year fixed mortgage rate at 7.11% for the week of Nov. 12, down from 7.18% on Nov. 5 and 7.40% on Oct. 8, a decline of 0.07 and 0.29 percentage points. It is the fourth straight weekly decline, and it came with the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.10% on Nov. 12, so the next weekly readings will show whether higher yields interrupt the trend.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (Freddie Mac)

items.headline: EIA: oil flows through Middle East chokepoints up 19% in Q3 2026
items.take: EIA said collective oil shipments through key Middle East chokepoints rose 19% in the third quarter of 2026, based on its Global Energy Security Data. The measure sums crude oil and petroleum product flows through the Strait of Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb and the Suez Canal/SUMED pipeline, and includes oil from countries outside the Middle East. The figure is a volume measure rather than a price signal, so it says nothing by itself about where oil prices go next.
items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration (Today in Energy)

items.headline: High-yield spread 3.47 points on Nov. 18, up from 3.20 on Nov. 12
items.take: FRED shows the ICE BofA US High Yield option-adjusted spread at 3.47 percentage points on Nov. 18, up 0.04 from Nov. 17 and 0.27 from Nov. 12. The investment-grade spread was 0.93, up 0.01 on the day. The high-yield spread has risen in each of the last four observations, which makes the next prints worth watching for whether credit is following rates.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (ICE Data Indices)

items.headline: UK regulators propose cyber guidance; October incidents 52% above prior peak
items.take: The Bank of England, FCA and PRA proposed guidance on how financial firms should prepare for and recover from cyber incidents, with a consultation closing Feb. 26, 2027. The Bank said October 2026 had the second-highest monthly count of cyber incidents reported to the FCA in five years, 52% above the previous 18-month peak recorded in May 2025. Separate effective-practice materials cover AI and quantum risks. The Bank's latest Systemic Risk Survey cited cyber among the risks with the greatest impact on the UK financial system.
items.source_name: Bank of England

items.headline: Jobless claims 203,000 in week ended Nov. 14; four-week average 197,750
items.take: The Labor Department reported seasonally adjusted initial claims of 203,000 for the week ending November 14, up 1,000 from the prior week's revised 202,000. The four-week moving average was 197,750, up 2,000 from a revised 195,750. AlphaGen read: claims remain near 200,000, with no sign of a layoff wave in this report.
items.source_name: U.S. Department of Labor (Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims, Nov. 19, 2026)

items.headline: Jefferson: inflation was already above 2% target when energy shock hit
items.take: Vice Chair Jefferson, speaking in Brasília on Nov. 19, said: "When the recent energy price shock occurred, inflation in the U.S. was already above our 2 percent target." He added that if inflation expectations risk becoming unanchored, "a stronger reaction to inflation is warranted." AlphaGen read: the speech frames expectations as the main test for how the Fed treats an energy-driven price jump.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board (Vice Chair Jefferson speech, Nov. 19, 2026)

items.headline: Continuing claims rise 70,000 to 1.763 million; insured rate 1.1%
items.take: The Labor Department said insured unemployment was 1,763,000 for the week ending November 7, up 70,000 from a revised 1,693,000, with the insured unemployment rate at 1.1% (unchanged). Unadjusted initial claims for the week ending November 14 were 197,492, versus 218,228 a year earlier, about 9.5% lower by AlphaGen's calculation. AlphaGen read: the continuing-claims increase is the more notable move in an otherwise low-claims report.
items.source_name: U.S. Department of Labor (Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims, Nov. 19, 2026)

items.headline: Jefferson: AI buildout is adding upward pressure on demand and inflation
items.take: In his Nov. 19 speech, Vice Chair Jefferson said: "Currently, the AI buildout is exerting upward pressure on demand and inflation." He also said "AI could cause some job displacement, a meaningful challenge for affected households." AlphaGen read: the Fed is weighing AI investment as both a demand source and a labor-market risk.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board (Vice Chair Jefferson speech, Nov. 19, 2026)

items.headline: Jefferson: goal is price stability with a solid labor market
items.take: Vice Chair Jefferson said: "For the U.S. economy, my goal is to restore price stability while maintaining a solid labor market." He also said "If price pressures are contained, it may be prudent to prioritize downside risks to employment." AlphaGen read: the conditional wording ties any shift toward employment risks to inflation first being contained.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board (Vice Chair Jefferson speech, Nov. 19, 2026)

items.headline: CPI: fuel oil +2.0% in October after +15.3% in September
items.take: BLS's October CPI shows fuel oil up 2.0% on the month after a 15.3% rise in September and 10.1% in August; June and July were declines of 9.2% and 1.7%. Compounding the seven monthly readings from April through October gives about 26.9% cumulatively, by AlphaGen's calculation. AlphaGen read: fuel oil rose again in October but at a much slower pace than in August and September.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (CPI news release, Nov. 10, 2026)

items.headline: CPI: piped gas -0.8% in October, third straight decline; electricity +0.9%
items.take: BLS reports the October CPI natural gas (utility, piped) index fell 0.8%, after declines of 0.3% in September and 1.1% in August, while electricity rose 0.9% and energy services overall rose 0.6%. The three monthly declines compound to about 2.2%, by AlphaGen's calculation. AlphaGen read: home-heating gas and electricity moved in opposite directions in October.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (CPI news release, Nov. 10, 2026)

items.headline: CPI groceries: other food +0.7%, produce and dairy +0.6% each, beverages -0.3%
items.take: Within October's 0.4% rise in food at home, BLS says four of the six major grocery groups increased: other food at home rose 0.7% (snacks +1.0%), meats, poultry, fish and eggs 0.5% (beef +0.9%), and fruits and vegetables and dairy 0.6% each. Nonalcoholic beverages fell 0.3% after rising 0.9% in September, and cereals and bakery products were unchanged. AlphaGen read: the October grocery gain was broad across groups rather than concentrated in one.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (CPI news release, Nov. 10, 2026)

items.headline: Real hourly earnings unchanged in October as pay and CPI both rose 0.4%
items.take: BLS says real average hourly earnings for all employees were unchanged from September to October, as a 0.4% rise in average hourly earnings matched a 0.4% rise in CPI-U; real weekly earnings were also unchanged. For production and nonsupervisory employees, real hourly earnings rose 0.1% (pay +0.4%, CPI-W +0.3%). BLS notes year-over-year comparisons are unavailable because October 2025 CPI data could not be collected during the 2025 lapse in appropriations. AlphaGen read: pay kept pace with prices on the month for the broad workforce.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (Real Earnings news release, Nov. 10, 2026)

items.headline: CPI core detail: recreation +0.8%, education +0.3%, communication -0.1%
items.take: BLS's October CPI shows recreation up 0.8% after 0.5% in September, motor vehicle insurance up 0.7%, education up 0.3% and household furnishings and operations up 0.2%, while communication fell 0.1% and used cars and trucks fell 1.2%. The index excluding food and energy rose 0.3% for a third straight month. AlphaGen read: recreation and insurance did most of the lifting among the categories BLS names as increases.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (CPI news release, Nov. 10, 2026)

items.headline: PPI: processed goods ex food and energy up 0.9% in October; energy goods down 1.6%
items.take: BLS's October PPI says processed goods for intermediate demand rose 0.4%, with processed materials less foods and energy up 0.9%, processed foods and feeds up 1.0% and processed energy goods down 1.6%. The 12-month rise for processed goods was 14.6%. AlphaGen read: the small headline gain hid a firmer non-energy core, which energy goods offset.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (PPI news release, Nov. 13, 2026)

items.headline: PPI: processed goods ex food and energy compound to about 8.4% since December
items.take: BLS's Table B shows processed goods for intermediate demand less foods and energy rising 0.5, 0.8, 0.8, 1.6, 1.7, 0.7, 0.1, 0.5, 0.5 and 0.9% from January through October, with no monthly decline. Compounding those rounded figures gives roughly 8.4% (AlphaGen calculation), against about 5.7% for total final demand on the same basis. AlphaGen read: October's 0.9% was the largest monthly gain since May's 1.7%.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (PPI news release, Nov. 13, 2026)

items.headline: PPI: metals wholesaling margins jumped 9.2% in October, driving services for intermediate demand
items.take: BLS says services for intermediate demand rose 0.6% in October, and thirty percent of the increase traced to a 9.2% jump in margins for metals, minerals and ores wholesaling. Nonresidential property management fees decreased 5.9%, and transportation and warehousing services for intermediate demand rose 1.2%. AlphaGen read: one wholesaling category accounted for roughly a third of the advance, so the broad gain leaned on a single margin line.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (PPI news release, Nov. 13, 2026)

items.headline: PPI: unprocessed nonfood materials ex energy fell 0.9% in October; raw milk rose 8.2%
items.take: BLS's October PPI shows unprocessed nonfood materials less energy down 0.9% and unprocessed foodstuffs and feedstuffs down 0.2%, with corn, slaughter hogs, wheat, aluminum base scrap and hay and hayseeds lower. Raw milk advanced 8.2%, and natural gas and carbon steel scrap also rose. AlphaGen read: outside energy, raw-material prices were mostly lower in October, with dairy and a few inputs the exceptions.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (PPI news release, Nov. 13, 2026)

items.headline: EIA: almost 70 Bcf more gas in storage by end-November than forecast in October
items.take: In a Nov. 10 release, EIA said it expects almost 70 billion cubic feet more natural gas in U.S. storage at the end of November than it forecast in October, after a warm start to the month. It put the Henry Hub spot price at an average of $2.87 per million Btu for November through March, 16% below last month's forecast; EIA's table labels the figures a draft subject to final review. AlphaGen read: FRED's Henry Hub spot was $3.10 on Nov. 17, above that forecast average.
items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration (press release, Nov. 10, 2026)

items.headline: EIA draft: Brent $104 in November, $99 in December, $86 average in 2027
items.take: EIA's Nov. 10 release forecasts Brent at $104 per barrel in November and $99 in December, with an $86 average in 2027; its table shows $97 for 2026. It sees retail gasoline at $3.73 per gallon in 2027 (October forecast: $3.56) and diesel at $5.03 (October: $4.49). AlphaGen read: FRED's Brent spot was $92.94 on Nov. 17, $11.06 below EIA's November figure; the EIA table is marked as a draft subject to final review.
items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration (press release, Nov. 10, 2026)

items.headline: EIA sees record U.S. crude output of 14.3 million b/d in 2027; LNG exports near 19 Bcf/d
items.take: EIA's Nov. 10 release shows U.S. crude oil production of 13.7 million barrels per day in 2025, 13.9 in 2026 and a record 14.3 in 2027. U.S. LNG gross exports go from about 15 billion cubic feet per day in 2025 to about 19 in 2027. AlphaGen read: the forecast pairs rising oil output with expanding LNG export volume over the same span; EIA labels the table a draft.
items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration (press release, Nov. 10, 2026)

items.headline: EIA: record U.S. power generation of almost 4,390 billion kWh in 2026, up 2.7%
items.take: EIA's Nov. 10 release puts 2026 U.S. electricity generation at a record of almost 4,390 billion kilowatthours, up 2.7% from 2025. Solar's share of generation is shown at 7% in 2025, 8% in 2026 and 10% in 2027, while natural gas is 40%, 40% and 39%. AlphaGen read: the table shows solar taking share over the period while gas slips one point by 2027.
items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration (press release, Nov. 10, 2026)

items.headline: Fed calendar today: Jefferson at 9:25 a.m., Barr on AI at 2:15 p.m., H.4.1 at 4:30 p.m.
items.take: The Federal Reserve's November calendar lists Vice Chair Jefferson in a discussion on "Economic Shocks" at an IMF and Central Bank of Brazil conference at 9:25 a.m. today, and Governor Barr in a discussion on artificial intelligence at the FinRegLab 2026 AI Symposium at 2:15 p.m. The H.4.1 balance sheet release is listed for 4:30 p.m. On Friday it lists Waller's welcoming remarks at the College Fed Challenge finals at 8:25 a.m. and Cook speaking in Santiago at 12:15 p.m. AlphaGen read: the calendar page gives no time zone, so check each event's own notice for local times.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board (calendar, November 2026)

items.headline: BLS December calendar: jobs Dec. 4, CPI Dec. 10, PPI Dec. 15, all 8:30 a.m. ET
items.take: BLS's December schedule lists the Employment Situation for November on Dec. 4, the Consumer Price Index and Real Earnings for November on Dec. 10, and the Producer Price Index for November on Dec. 15, each at 8:30 a.m. ET. JOLTS for October comes first, on Dec. 1 at 10:00 a.m. AlphaGen read: the jobs report comes six days before the CPI, so labor data arrives first.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (release calendar, December 2026)

items.headline: FRED: 2-year up 24 bp, 10-year up 22 bp since Nov. 9
items.take: FRED shows the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.80% on Nov. 17 versus 4.56% on Nov. 9, a rise of 24 basis points. The 10-year went from 4.88% to 5.10% (22 bp) and the 30-year from 5.26% to 5.46% (20 bp; AlphaGen calculations). AlphaGen read: the front end rose slightly more than the long end over the span, so the move was a broad shift up rather than a steepening.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (DGS2, DGS10, DGS30)

items.headline: Waller: stablecoins already settle obligations among card-network participants
items.take: Governor Waller said in his Nov. 17 speech that stablecoins are starting to be used behind the scenes to settle obligations among participants in card networks. He added that The Clearing House is one of several groups building a network for clearing and settling tokenized deposits. AlphaGen read: the speech frames tokenization as an extension of existing payment plumbing, not only of crypto-asset trading.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board (Waller speech, Nov. 17, 2026)

items.headline: FRED: 30-year yield 0.36 pt above 10-year on Nov. 17, versus 0.38 on Nov. 9
items.take: FRED shows the 30-year Treasury yield at 5.46% and the 10-year at 5.10% on Nov. 17, a gap of 0.36 percentage point. On Nov. 9 the yields were 5.26% and 4.88%, a gap of 0.38 (AlphaGen calculations). AlphaGen read: the long end has kept its small premium over the 10-year as both rose.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (DGS10, DGS30)

items.headline: Waller: tokenized assets must keep legal identity, ownership rights across networks
items.take: Governor Waller said assets that move across networks must maintain legal identity, ownership rights, economic terms, compliance obligations, corporate-action treatment, and access to liquidity. He said clear legal treatment of tokenized claims, settlement records, custody, insolvency, and resolution will be critical to mainstream institutional adoption. AlphaGen read: the Fed governor put legal and governance clarity ahead of technology as the hurdle for scale.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board (Waller speech, Nov. 17, 2026)

items.headline: FRED: Fed reverse repo usage $0.331B on Nov. 18, from $0.351B a day earlier
items.take: FRED shows overnight reverse repurchase agreement usage at $0.331 billion on Nov. 18, versus $0.351 billion on Nov. 17 and $0.182 billion on Nov. 16. On Nov. 10 it was $0.152 billion. AlphaGen read: usage remains a tiny fraction of the Fed's $6.76 trillion balance sheet (WALCL, Nov. 11), so the facility is not a meaningful liquidity sink.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (RRPONTSYD)

items.headline: Barr cites Syracuse housing fund: $30M seed money plus $120M from private partners
items.take: Barr's Nov. 18 speech highlighted Syracuse, New York, which announced earlier this year a revolving loan fund for mixed-income housing. The fund provided $30 million in seed money, and a group of private partners contributed the remaining $120 million, which totals $150 million. AlphaGen read: a 4-to-1 private-to-public split is the kind of partnership Barr said can overcome market failures in low-income areas.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board (Barr speech, Nov. 18, 2026)

items.headline: Barr: LIHTC created or preserved nearly 4 million housing units in 40 years
items.take: Governor Barr said the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit has helped create or preserve nearly 4 million units of housing over the past 40 years. He also said the bipartisan New Markets Tax Credit, which he helped launch a quarter century ago, was recently made permanent by Congress. AlphaGen read: the speech frames tax-credit financing as a core tool for community investment.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board (Barr speech, Nov. 18, 2026)

items.headline: Barr: 44% of Americans live in low-income communities; most households hold little wealth
items.take: In a Nov. 18 speech, Fed Governor Michael Barr cited recent estimates that 44 percent of Americans live in low-income communities, where a fifth or more of people live below the poverty line. He said the Fed's recent Survey of Consumer Finances confirms that the majority of households has very little wealth, and that lower-wealth households are nearly four times as likely to say they cannot rely on friends and family for financial help. AlphaGen read: Barr paired a strong-economy view with a warning that gains are uneven.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board (Barr speech, Nov. 18, 2026)

items.headline: BoE market group: energy prices and market rates correlated; views split on shock effects
items.take: According to the MPG minutes, participants noted the correlation between energy prices and market rates and how it has evolved over recent months. Views differed on the relative importance of the energy shock's demand-side and supply-side effects, and participants noted the distinction between market-curve pricing and modal expectations for policy. AlphaGen read: the group did not agree on whether the energy shock is mainly a demand or a supply story.
items.source_name: Bank of England (Market Participants Group minutes, Nov. 18, 2026)

items.headline: BoE market group flags AI debt financing, hedge-fund leverage, sovereign and cyber risks
items.take: The Bank of England's MPG minutes say participants noted the support to global growth from AI-related capital expenditure and discussed the increasing role of debt financing, plus the implications of a change in AI expectations for risky asset markets. They also covered potential vulnerabilities from elevated hedge-fund leverage, sovereign debt pressures and cyber risks. AlphaGen read: the concerns echo the AI-debt themes raised by Fed and ECB officials this week.
items.source_name: Bank of England (Market Participants Group minutes, Nov. 18, 2026)

items.headline: BoE market group: UK growth resilience 'strengthened the case for higher rates'
items.take: Minutes of the Bank of England's Market Participants Group meeting of Nov. 18, published Nov. 19, say participants noted the resilience of UK growth this year despite the energy shock. That resilience was broadly seen to have strengthened the case for higher rates, with the November increase having been widely expected. AlphaGen read: the group's view is that the move to 4% was anticipated rather than a surprise.
items.source_name: Bank of England (Market Participants Group minutes, Nov. 18, 2026)

items.headline: FOMC minutes: rate held at 3-3/4 to 4%, 10-2 vote; Cook, Hammack wanted a hike
items.take: The minutes of the Oct. 27-28 meeting say the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent, approved by a 10-2 vote. Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack voted against, preferring to raise the target range by 1/4 percentage point at that meeting. AlphaGen read: two dissents in favor of a hike show the debate at the Committee was about tightening, not easing.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board (FOMC minutes, Oct. 27-28, 2026)

items.headline: FOMC minutes: almost all participants saw a further rate increase as likely appropriate
items.take: The minutes say almost all participants judged that, under their baseline outlooks for inflation and the labor market, further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent objective. Most participants expressed support for maintaining the range at the October meeting. AlphaGen read: the minutes point to a Committee debating when to raise rates, not whether.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board (FOMC minutes, Oct. 27-28, 2026)

items.headline: FOMC minutes: some wanted 25 bp in October; a couple floated more than 25 bp next
items.take: According to the minutes, some participants favored a 25 basis point increase at the October meeting, and a few who backed holding called it a close call. A couple of participants noted that an increase of more than 25 basis points could warrant consideration at the next meeting if incoming inflation data were unfavorable. items.headline: ECB: risks elevated; non-bank vulnerabilities more pronounced, safeguards less developed
items.take: In the Nov. 18 Financial Stability Review release, Vice-President Boris Vujčić said risks to euro area financial stability "remain elevated, given persistent geoeconomic uncertainty and growing exposure to AI." He said banks are "well placed to withstand shocks, while vulnerabilities are more pronounced in certain non-banks where risks are growing and macroprudential safeguards are less developed." AlphaGen read: the ECB is drawing a line between a bank sector it calls resilient and non-bank pockets where it sees thinner safeguards.
items.source_name: ECB

items.headline: October CPI: owners' equivalent rent +0.3%, rent +0.2%, lodging away from home +0.6%
items.take: BLS's October CPI, released Nov. 10, shows shelter rose 0.3 percent, accounting for over thirty percent of the monthly all-items increase. Within it, owners' equivalent rent rose 0.3 percent, rent increased 0.2 percent, and lodging away from home rose 0.6 percent after a 2.0 percent rise in September. AlphaGen read: rent and owners' equivalent rent moved in a narrow range, so the lodging swing was the more volatile part of shelter.
items.source_name: BLS

items.headline: ECB: euro area resilient despite energy shock; prolonged supply disruption could test it
items.take: The ECB's Nov. 18 Financial Stability Review release says the euro area economy has continued to demonstrate resilience despite an energy shock, trade frictions and extreme weather events. It adds that prolonged energy supply disruptions and persistent trade policy uncertainty could test that resilience, and that higher energy prices and weaker economic conditions could make it harder for households and firms to repay debts. AlphaGen read: the ECB ties the energy backdrop directly to loan repayment risk, even while saying bank asset quality remains sound.
items.source_name: ECB

items.headline: October CPI: snacks +1.0%, beef +0.9%; nonalcoholic beverages -0.3% after +0.9%
items.take: BLS's October CPI, released Nov. 10, shows the food index rose 0.5 percent after being unchanged in September, with food at home up 0.4 percent. Other food at home rose 0.7 percent as snacks rose 1.0 percent, and the beef index rose 0.9 percent. Nonalcoholic beverages fell 0.3 percent after rising 0.9 percent in September, and cereals and bakery products were unchanged. AlphaGen read: the grocery increase was concentrated in a few groups rather than broad.
items.source_name: BLS

items.headline: ECB: AI financing, sovereign bond exposures leave banks, non-banks open to repricing
items.take: The ECB's Nov. 18 Financial Stability Review release says banks' and non-banks' exposures to AI financing and sovereign bonds leave them exposed to repricing risks, and that closer links between banks and non-banks could spread and amplify shocks across the financial system. It also says the banking sector is well positioned to absorb shocks, with strong profits, solid capital buffers and ample liquidity. AlphaGen read: the ECB's concern is transmission between banks and non-banks, not bank capital.
items.source_name: ECB

items.headline: October CPI: recreation +0.8%, motor vehicle insurance +0.7%, hospital services +0.8%
items.take: BLS's October CPI, released Nov. 10, shows the recreation index increased 0.8 percent after rising 0.5 percent in September, and the motor vehicle insurance index rose 0.7 percent. The medical care index increased 0.3 percent after 0.1 percent in September, with hospital services up 0.8 percent, physicians' services up 0.4 percent and prescription drugs up 0.3 percent. AlphaGen read: services categories outside shelter contributed several of the larger monthly gains.
items.source_name: BLS

items.headline: ECB priorities: bank resilience, non-bank liquidity; backs savings and investments union
items.take: The ECB's Nov. 18 Financial Stability Review release says preserving bank resilience remains a key macroprudential priority, alongside addressing vulnerabilities related to liquidity and high levels of borrowing among some non-banks. It adds that accelerating progress on the EU's savings and investments union will be essential to support economic growth and competitiveness while preserving financial stability. AlphaGen read: the ECB pairs near-term supervisory priorities with a structural capital-markets agenda.
items.source_name: ECB

items.headline: EIA: U.S. energy supply and demand gap was about 0.3% in 2025
items.take: EIA said its surveys put U.S. total primary energy supply and demand each at about 128 quadrillion Btu in 2025, with "stock change and other" at 0.4 quads, about 0.3% of the total. EIA uses over 60 surveys and says supply should balance demand in theory but small differences appear in practice. AlphaGen read: the gap is small relative to the market, though EIA presents it as a measure of survey uncertainty.
items.source_name: EIA, Today in Energy (Nov. 17, 2026)

items.headline: EIA explains how it reconciles energy supply and demand: stock change plus other
items.take: EIA's Monthly Energy Review defines supply as production plus imports and demand as consumption plus exports, with demand minus supply equal to stock change plus other. Stock change is the net difference between energy in storage at the start and end of a month. AlphaGen read: the monthly balance is closed by this accounting line, so small revisions can show up there.
items.source_name: EIA, Today in Energy (Nov. 17, 2026)

items.headline: EIA lists sources of energy data mismatches: timing, reporting practices, estimation errors
items.take: EIA says the "other" part of its supply-demand reconciliation covers differences in respondent accounting and reporting practices, timing between energy activity and reporting periods, measurement and estimation errors, limits in survey coverage, energy lost in transfers or storage, and unreported activities. EIA says these series are standard statistical accounting and not a flaw in the underlying data. AlphaGen read: users of EIA balances should expect small unexplained residuals.
items.source_name: EIA, Today in Energy (Nov. 17, 2026)

items.headline: EIA: petroleum, gas and coal each use their own balancing series
items.take: EIA says petroleum and biofuels use an adjustments series because survey responses may not match actual activity, natural gas uses a balancing item (including gas lost to the atmosphere and conversion differences), and coal uses a losses and unaccounted for series. EIA also says that in 2009, because of incomplete data coverage and different source data, biofuels have a small balancing item. AlphaGen read: each fuel's residual has a different cause, so they are not interchangeable.
items.source_name: EIA, Today in Energy (Nov. 17, 2026)

items.headline: ECB: AI valuations rely on ambitious earnings; debt funding widens spillover risk
items.take: The ECB's November 2026 Financial Stability Review said current AI valuations rely on ambitious earnings expectations that could be challenged by financing concerns or competition from cheaper AI models. It noted that AI infrastructure investment is increasingly funded through debt, so a change in sentiment could spread losses from equity markets to bond markets. AlphaGen read: the ECB is treating AI financing as a cross-asset channel, not only an equity-valuation question.
items.source_name: European Central Bank

items.headline: ECB flags abrupt sovereign repricing risk; says euro area banks well placed
items.take: The ECB said elevated debt levels, growing sovereign borrowing needs and a shift toward more news-sensitive, leveraged investors in euro area sovereign bonds raise the risk of abrupt repricing episodes, though markets have continued to function in an orderly manner. It added that the banking sector is well positioned to absorb shocks, underpinned by strong profits, solid capital buffers and ample liquidity. Vice-President Boris Vujcic said vulnerabilities are more pronounced in certain non-banks. AlphaGen read: the ECB places the weaker safeguards outside the banking system.
items.source_name: European Central Bank

items.take: BLS reported real average hourly earnings for production and nonsupervisory employees rose 0.1% from September to October, as a 0.4% increase in hourly earnings outpaced a 0.3% rise in the CPI-W. items.headline: Transportation and warehousing +25,000 in October; couriers +71,000 since February
items.take: BLS reported transportation and warehousing added 25,000 jobs in October, with couriers and messengers up 17,000 and air transportation up 4,000. items.headline: Manufacturing added 19,000 jobs in October, 101,000 since December 2025 low
items.take: BLS reported manufacturing employment rose by 19,000 in October and has increased by 101,000 since a recent low in December 2025, with gains in computer and electronic products (+7,000), machinery (+4,000) and primary metals (+4,000). items.headline: Labor force participation 61.9%, employment-population ratio 59.3% in October
items.take: BLS reported a labor force participation rate of 61.9% and an employment-population ratio of 59.3% in October, both little changed, and says both have shown little net change since January. items.headline: Part-time for economic reasons up 339,000 to 4.8M in October

items.headline: Long-term unemployed 2.0M in October, 27.6% of all jobless people

items.take: BLS reported Nov. 17 that U.S. import prices increased 1.1 percent in October after a 1.1 percent rise in September, while export prices rose 1.1 percent in October after a 2.4 percent rise in September.
